newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent bearish while under $18.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent bearish while under $18.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+Brent is looking bearish while it remains under the key $18 mark. This will form resistance, and above that lies another layer at $18.08.
+Most important support lies at around $17.50 a barrel.
IPE Brent crude oil futures were looking bearish on Friday and traders and technical analysts said they saw $18 as the key number to break if the market is to recover.
August Brent closed 26 cents a barrel lower on Thursday at $17.96, while gas oil's July contract, which is the new front month, closed $11.50 down at $161.75.
Nicola Merrell at MMS in London said that the settlement below $18 a barrel on Thursday was significant and this lent the Brent market a bearish hue.
"As long as the $18 level holds as resistance then this should continue pushing lower," she said, adding that her daily momentum indicators were pointing to further losses.

She pegged support at $17.49, the low point reached on the August contract chart on June 20. Beneath that she said the next level of congestion on the August chart lay at $17.13, dating from nearly a year ago.
Other traders, looking at the spot month continuation chart, saw support also at $17.32, a significant low formed on June 11.

But Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore, examining his own momentum indicators, said: "The market...may struggle to move lower today as the RSIs are looking oversold on a short term basis."
He pegged support at $17.50 a barrel, a couple of cents above the contract low formed on the August chart on June 20.
